Indian

SPECIFICATION FOR STENCIL TEMPLATES AND PEN TIPS FOR ENGLISH LETTERING
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 7 August 1986, after the draft finalized by the Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 0.2 This standard deals with mechanical type cut-through stencil templates and pen tips for English lettering used extensively in drawing o&ces for writing numerals and letterings on drawings and charts for characters having line thickness to height ratio of 1 : 10 and 1 : 14. 0.3 Taking into consideration the views of producers and consumers the sectional committee responsible for the preparation of this standard felt that it should be related to the manufacturing practices followed in the country in this field. 0.4 Metric system has been adopted in India standard have been given in this system. and all the values in this

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 0.6 This standard is intended chiefly to cover the technical provisions relating to stencil templates and pen tips, and it does not include all the necessary provisions of a contract.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements stencil templates and pen tips for English of mechanical lettering. type cut-through

3.3 In case of pattern C templates the dhannels shall be made from hard plastics. 4.1 The grooves for letter, numerals and other symbols on the templates shall be such as to reproduce these characters in conformity with IS : 96091983*. The concerned recommended permissible tolerances have been given in Table 1 for characters having line thickness to height ratio of I : 10 and in Table 2 for characters having such ratio of I : 14. 4.2 Stencil templates shall be rectangular in shape having fully mouldcd milled or machined edges. The composite templates shall have plastic or metallic channels on the two long edges. 4.3 The grooving shall be in straight parallel to each other. line along long edges which shall be

4.4 The templates shall normally have two grooved lines with capital letters and numerals in one line and lower case ( small ) letters and mathematical symbols in the other line. 4.5 Stencil templates with 14 and 20 mm letter heights may be made in more than one piece so as to cover all capital IetterS, numerals, lower case letters and mathematical symbols. 4.6 Minimum gap between the paper surface and the bottom of the grooved portion of the template shall be one millimetre, when kept in the working position. 4.7 Minimum blank space on tither side of characters shall bc 10 mm. template template to the shall

4.10 The recommended sizes of the pen tips to be used with the stencil templates shall be as given in Table 1 and Table 2 read with Fig. 5. The diameter d, of the tip shall be such that with the pen held vertically and the line drawn at a speed of 2 to .4 cm/s, the tolerances for the line widths shall not exceed f 10 percent of diameter d,. For this purpose, the ink recommended by the manufacturer and the smooth tracing paper 90-95 g/m* shall be used.

4.11 The detailed design of the pen shall be left to the manufacturer as it covers the requirements of pen tips given in 4.10.

4.12 Stencil template and pen tip shall match with each other to ensure proper working.
5. WORKMANSHIP 5.1 The characters AND FINISH

shall be uniformly and neatly grooved or moulded. The workmanship and finish shall be of the best grade and to the entire satisfaction of purchaser. 6. TESTS
6.1 The templates

and pen tips shall he tested to conform to the rcquirements given under 3. 4 and 5.

7. MARKING
7.1 The stencil templates and the pens shall be marked with the manufacturer's name or trade-mark and the year of manufacture.

Additional size of 25 mm stencil template may also be manufactured if agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer with the permissible tolerances as given in Tables 1 and 2 at St No. 8. 14 mm and 20 mm templates are manufactured in 4 parts (each of 350 mm length), whereas 25 mm template can be made in 5 parts, without increasing the length of the template.

IS : 11781- 1986 7.1.1 The templates shall also be marked with the pattern of template, the height of the character, d/h ratio and the size of the pen to be used while the pen shall be marked with its size. 7.1.2 The templates may also be marked with the Standard Mark.

NOTE-The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked nroducts are also continuouslv checked bv BIS for conformity to that Detafis of conditions under which a hcence for standard=as a further safeguard. the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
